## Diagnosis

`get_environment_proxies()` classifies `fe11::/16` as IPv6 because `is_ipv6_hostname()` validates only the substring before `/`. It then constructs:

```text
all://[fe11::/16]
```

The CIDR suffix is therefore placed inside the IPv6 brackets. `URLPattern` passes that malformed URL to `URL(pattern)`, whose authority parsing eventually interprets part of the colon sequence as a port and raises `InvalidURL: Invalid port: ':'`. This occurs while both synchronous and asynchronous clients construct their proxy-mount dictionaries, before any request is sent.

Changing the spelling to `all://[fe11::]/16` would prevent the constructor failure but would not, by itself, implement CIDR behavior: ordinary URL parsing treats `/16` as a path, while `URLPattern.matches()` currently compares only scheme, host regex, and port. The existing IPv4 case `all://192.168.0.0/16` consequently appears likely to match only `192.168.0.0`, not every address in that network. That inference is based solely on the excerpt; unseen `URL` normalization could alter the exact symptom but not the absence of explicit network-membership logic shown here.

## Minimal change design

Keep the change localized to proxy-pattern construction and `URLPattern` in `_utils.py`; both client classes already share that path.

- Validate slash-bearing IP values as complete networks with `ipaddress.ip_network(..., strict=False)`, rather than validating only the text before `/`.
- Emit syntactically valid IPv6 URL keys by bracketing only the address: `all://[fe11::]/16`. Preserve existing keys for hostnames, IPv4, bare IPv6, wildcard, scheme-qualified, localhost, and port forms.
- Have `URLPattern` recognize a CIDR suffix from the original pattern and retain an `IPv4Network` or `IPv6Network`.
- In `matches()`, apply the existing scheme and port checks, then parse `other.host` as an IP address and test network membership. A hostname or opposite-family address must not match.
- Preserve the current regex path and priority calculation unchanged for every non-network pattern.
- Give network patterns deterministic ordering ahead of scheme-only fallbacks; overlapping networks should order most-specific prefix first. Exact host and port-constrained behavior must retain existing precedence.
- Normalize host-bit-set CIDRs with `strict=False`, or reject them consistently. Normalization is the smaller compatibility-preserving choice because the existing classifiers already accept them by examining only their address portion.

No client-specific change should be necessary: the shared `URLPattern` construction automatically covers `Client` and `AsyncClient`.

## Regression matrix

| Input or pattern | Candidate URL | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| `no_proxy=fe11::/16` | client construction | Succeeds; produces a valid network-aware bypass mount |
| `fe11::/16` | `http://[fe11::1]/` | Bypass |
| `fe11::/16` | `https://[fe11:ffff::1]/` | Bypass |
| `fe11::/16` | `http://[fe12::1]/` | Proxy |
| `fe11::/16` | `http://fe11.example/` | Proxy; textual resemblance is irrelevant |
| `fe11::/16` | `http://192.168.1.1/` | Proxy; IP families differ |
| `::/0` | any IPv6 literal | Bypass |
| `::/0` | any IPv4 literal or hostname | Proxy |
| `2001:db8::1/128` | exactly `2001:db8::1` | Bypass |
| `2001:db8::1/128` | adjacent IPv6 address | Proxy |
| `2001:db8::1/64` | address inside normalized `2001:db8::/64` | Bypass |
| `192.168.0.0/16` | `http://192.168.255.255/` | Bypass, covering the latent IPv4 CIDR case |
| `192.168.0.0/16` | `http://192.169.0.0/` | Proxy |
| `127.0.0.1` | `http://127.0.0.1/` | Existing exact-address bypass remains |
| `::1` | `http://[::1]/` | Existing exact-IPv6 bypass remains |
| `localhost` | `http://localhost/` | Existing bypass remains |
| `.example.com` or equivalent supported hostname form | matching subdomain and unrelated domain | Existing hostname semantics remain unchanged |
| `*` | any URL | Existing behavior remains an empty proxy map |
| scheme-qualified `NO_PROXY` entry | matching and nonmatching schemes | Existing scheme behavior remains |
| port-qualified hostname entry | matching and nonmatching ports | Existing port behavior remains |
| `/0`, `/32`, `/128` | relevant IP families | Valid boundary prefixes |
| IPv4 `/33`, IPv6 `/129`, nonnumeric suffix | client construction | Must not be mistaken for a valid network; behavior should be deliberate and non-ambiguous |
| exact host, CIDR, scheme-only proxy, and user mount together | URLs matching multiple entries | Exact/port-specific and more-specific network entries precede broader fallbacks; pre-existing non-network order is unchanged |
| every applicable case above | `Client` and `AsyncClient` | Identical mount construction and selection |

## Candidate residue

Reusable rule: when a configuration token embeds non-URL semantics inside a URL-shaped dispatch key, making it parseable is insufficient; the dispatcher must explicitly preserve and evaluate those semantics.

This applies when CIDRs or similar selectors are encoded into proxy/mount patterns. It does not apply when the downstream URL abstraction is documented to retain and match that selector natively.

## Confidence and disconfirmation

Confidence: **0.91**.

The diagnosis would be disproved or materially changed if the complete source shows that `URL` treats CIDR paths as network selectors, that another layer converts CIDRs before `URLPattern.matches()`, or that proxy bypass occurs outside the shown mount mechanism. Evidence that IPv4 CIDRs already match arbitrary in-network addresses without additional logic would specifically invalidate the inferred latent IPv4 defect and require locating that unseen membership implementation. The minimal design would also need revision if public compatibility requires preserving malformed slash-bearing entries, supports CIDR-plus-port syntax, or defines a different precedence for overlapping networks.
